task_card.title: The plugin entity grows up - a dropdown entry, plugin-owned controls, and a plugin a Flow can require

next_action.description: Start MPI-579 (LTX Video upscaler) - read its card description, which is current and thorough, then write its plan.md. The mechanism it was blocked on is DONE: declare `upscale: { kinds: ['video'], label: 'LTX Video upscaler', fields: [...] }` on the new PluginDef and the dropdown entry, its controls and the hidden 0-1 mapping all come for free - a slider needs only `mapTo: [0.50, 0.85]`. What MPI-579 still has to build is the plugin definition itself, its commandRegistry op, the app-side v2v workflow off MPI-568's proven build_v2v.py, audio pass-through, and the in-app VRAM measurement that decides whether this runs in the app at all.

key_decisions: PLUGINS DO NOT GET SPECIAL CASES. Fabio, 2026-08-19: 'Plug-ins shouldn't differ just because of this or that. The plugin needs X, Y, and Z, so the plugin will need to install X, Y, and Z. If X, Y, and Z are already installed because LTX is installed, then the plugin is already installed.' This killed an invented product question about the Library row and an invented GC redesign. The precedent is live in the shipped build: the image describer's encoder is also a Krea2 dep.

ONE CONTROL VOCABULARY, ONE RENDERER. A plugin's controls are `FlowStepField` verbatim (MPI-572), rendered by the extracted js/utils/declaredFields.js. Copying the renderer was rejected because that is precisely the two-surface bug MPI-572 was written to kill - and the Flow twin of this capability would have made it a third copy.

`mapTo` IS APPLIED AT PAYLOAD TIME, NEVER AT WIDGET TIME. The stored and persisted value is always the declared 0-1 one, so a restored control seeds correctly and no inverse mapping exists anywhere in the codebase.

FLOWS ARE THE BEGINNER SURFACE AND DUPLICATION IS DELIBERATE. The same capability ships as a workspace tool AND as a Flow so a non-technical user never leaves the Flow Library. An agent finding the same capability twice must not 'fix' it by deleting one. Recorded in memory as project_flows_are_the_beginner_surface.
constraints: `[hidden]` DOES NOT HIDE an element whose class gives it `display:flex` - the UA rule loses. It cost one wrong screenshot in this session (Upscale Factor stayed visible under a plugin entry, and the plugin's controls would have leaked under None). The `__section[hidden]` rule in MpiToolOptionsUpscale.css is load-bearing, not tidiness. DOM assertions did not catch it; the screenshot did.

The Bash tool BLOCKS heredocs - write python with the Write tool and run it by path. Board/event writes must use the {schema,id,type,at,actor,summary} shape or the validator fails two ways per line.

NEVER take Fabio's app instance. `npm run app:isolated` spins your own; its READY line never reaches the background output file (buffering), so read the port out of the profile's app.log instead: %TEMP%/cubric-agent-profile/logs/app.log. Stopping it needs the process TREE - taskkill /PID <root> /T /F.

A REAL-PIXEL PROBE EARNS ITS COST HERE. Mounting the component in the live app with a fake viewer proved the whole chain (kind filtering, entry placement, controls, mapped payload) without needing a project with video history - and it was the SCREENSHOT, not the assertions, that found the only real bug.
